summary: Target-level plan of K-theory of schemes, localisation and operations, Part II: supported formal K-theory and derived intersection degrees. It extends SchemeKTheoryOperations from noetherian schemes to noetherian and locally noetherian formal schemes, after Appendix B of Zhang's proof of the arithmetic fundamental lemma, as Li–Zhang, Li–Liu and He–Li–Shi–Yang use it. FK.0 fixes the local algebra that formal schemes need and schemes hide: dimension and codimension through stalks rather than underlying spaces, regular and Cohen–Macaulay formal schemes, regular immersions, formal (power-of-the-ideal) support, and Tor sheaves. FK.1 defines K′_0 of coherent modules, the Gillet–Soulé group K_0^Y of strict complexes with formal support, the homology class map, the cup product and the Tor pairing, and transports everything on Spf A to Spec A. FK.2 proves the regular supported dévissage K_0^Y(X) ≅ K′_0(Y) under the resolution property, defines the codimension and dimension filtrations and compares them, proves rational multiplicativity (B.3) on affine regular formal schemes, and extends all groups to locally noetherian formal schemes by noetherian exhaustion. FK.3 proves Lemma B.1 (closed unions, with the cokernel and inverse-limit corrections) and Lemma B.2 (Tor vanishing in expected dimension, and componentwise with an expanded prime-level proof), and the pullback of Cartier divisor classes. FK.4 defines the Euler degree of schemes proper over Spf A and the derived Euler–Poincaré pairing (B.4), with base change, pushforward and projection formulas, the length-times-rank formula for zero-dimensional classes and the pairing with Cartier divisors. Multiplicativity of the codimension filtration on non-affine formal schemes is not claimed.

nodes.title: Stalks of Spf A, localisations of A and completed localisations share their completion
nodes.statement: Let A be a noetherian adic ring with ideal of definition I, X = Spf A, and let x ∈ |X| correspond to the open prime p ⊇ I. The canonical maps A_p → O_{X,x} → A{A∖p} (the last is the completed localisation lim_n (A/I^n)_p) are local homomorphisms of noetherian local rings, both flat, and each induces isomorphisms modulo I^n for every n ≥ 1: A_p/I^nA_p ≅ O_{X,x}/I^nO_{X,x} ≅ (A/I^n)_p. Consequently the three rings have isomorphic maximal-ideal-adic completions, and hence the same Krull dimension, and one of them is regular (respectively Cohen–Macaulay) if and only if all three are. Every maximal ideal of A contains I, so the closed points of |Spf A| are exactly the maximal ideals of A.
hypotheses: A noetherian and complete and separated for its I-adic topology (an adic noetherian ring, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).
x is a point of the formal spectrum, i.e. an open prime ideal p of A (p ⊇ I).
proofSteps: The stalk of the structure sheaf of Spf A at x is the colimit of the completed localisations A_{f} over f ∉ p (EGA I (10.1.5)); it is a noetherian local ring with residue field k(p) (EGA I (10.1.6)), and A_p → A{A∖p} is local and faithfully flat (EGA 0_I (7.6.17)–(7.6.18)). The map A_p → O_{X,x} is flat because it is the filtered colimit of the flat completed localisations; O_{X,x} → A{A∖p} is its I-adic completion map and is flat by EGA 0_I (7.6.16). The local maps are faithful.
Modulo I^n every term becomes the stalk of the scheme Spec(A/I^n) at p, namely (A/I^n)_p (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization: A_{f}/I^nA_{f} ≅ (A/I^n)_f, and colimits commute with quotients).

For a noetherian local ring R with maximal ideal m ⊇ I, R/m^n is a quotient of R/I^n by the image of m^n; hence two such rings with the same quotients R/I^n compatibly have the same m-adic completion.
Dimension, regularity and the Cohen–Macaulay property of a noetherian local ring are those of its completion (Stacks 07NV, 07NY, 07NX).
I-adic completeness puts I in the Jacobson radical of A (Stacks 05GI applied to the complete ring A), so every maximal ideal is open.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p⟦t⟧ and x the closed point, all three rings are ℤ_p⟦t⟧ itself.

For A = ℤ_p⟨t⟩ (p-adic completion of ℤ_p[t]) and p = (p), A_p is a discrete valuation ring, O_{X,x} is a discrete valuation ring with the same completion, and all have dimension 1, while the maximal ideals (p, f(t)) have height 2.

sources.match: The completed localisation at an open prime is a local ring, faithfully flat over the ordinary localisation when A is adic noetherian; the stalks of Spf A are the colimits of the completed localisations, noetherian local rings with residue field k(p).
A noetherian local ring and its completion have the same dimension, and one is regular, respectively Cohen–Macaulay, exactly when the other is.
For the completion of a ring along I, the extended ideal lies in the Jacobson radical; applied to an I-adically complete ring this puts I in every maximal ideal.

nodes.title: Local dimension and codimension on locally noetherian formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme). For x ∈ |X| put dim_x X := ringKrullDim O_{X,x} (a noetherian local ring), and dim X := sup_x dim_x X, with dim ∅ = ⊥. For noetherian X, X has pure dimension d if dim_x X = d at every closed point x of |X|. For a closed formal subscheme Z ⊆ X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme) and z ∈ |Z|, the local codimension is codim_z(Z, X) := dim O_{X,z} − dim O_{Z,z}, and codim_X Z := inf_{z ∈ |Z|} codim_z(Z, X) (= ⊤ for Z = ∅). These are dimensions of local rings, not topological dimensions of |X|: on X = Spf A, dim_x X = dim A_p for the open prime p of x, dim Spf A = ringKrullDim A, and dim Spf(A/𝔞) = ringKrullDim(A/𝔞) (FK.0/stalk-completion-comparison).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian, so every stalk is a noetherian local ring (EGA I (10.1.6)) and has finite Krull dimension.
Codimension is measured in the ambient X, never relative to an intermediate support.

IsPureDim is used here for noetherian X and finite d. This ensures that every point specialises to a closed point; the closed-point condition alone is not a purity convention on arbitrary locally noetherian spaces.
The local symbol dim_x means stalk dimension, not the infimum of dimensions of open neighbourhoods (the different convention of SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/local-dimension).
proofSteps: dim_x X is ringKrullDim of the stalk; on an affine formal open Spf A it equals dim A_p by FK.0/stalk-completion-comparison.

Every maximal ideal of A is a closed point of |Spf A| and dimensions of local rings increase under specialisation, so dim Spf A = sup over maximal ideals of dim A_m = ringKrullDim A; the same applied to A/𝔞 gives dim Spf(A/𝔞).

For a locally noetherian scheme Y regarded as a formal scheme, stalks are unchanged, so localDim (ofScheme Y) y = dim O_{Y,y}, and the global supremum agrees with the usual dimension of Y. This does not identify localDim with the supplier’s neighbourhood-dimension function: at the generic point of A¹_k those values are 0 and 1 respectively.
acceptance: dim Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧ = 2 although its underlying space is one point.
In Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧: codim V(t) = codim V(t − p) = 1, codim V(p, t) = 2, codim V(t(t − p)) = 1.

nodes.title: Regular and Cohen–Macaulay formal schemes
nodes.statement: A locally noetherian formal scheme X is regular (respectively Cohen–Macaulay) if every stalk O_{X,x}, x ∈ |X|, is a regular local ring in Mathlib's sense IsRegularLocalRing (respectively a Cohen–Macaulay local ring, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/cohen-macaulay). A closed formal subscheme is regular or Cohen–Macaulay when it is so as a formal scheme. For X = Spf A with A adic noetherian: X is regular if and only if A is a regular ring (IsRegularRing A), and Cohen–Macaulay if and only if every localisation of A at a maximal ideal is Cohen–Macaulay.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian.

Regularity is a condition on all stalks, closed or not; on each affine formal open it suffices to check the points given by maximal ideals of its coordinate ring. Globally closed points suffice when X is noetherian.
proofSteps: By FK.0/stalk-completion-comparison, O_{X,x} is regular (Cohen–Macaulay) iff A_p is, for the open prime p of x.

Every maximal ideal of A is open (I lies in the Jacobson radical), and localisations of regular local rings are regular (Stacks 0AFS) and of Cohen–Macaulay local rings are Cohen–Macaulay, so the condition at all open primes is equivalent to the condition at all primes, i.e. IsRegularRing A.
Regular local rings are domains (Stacks 00NP) and Cohen–Macaulay (Stacks 00O7 with depth = dimension).
acceptance: Spf ℤ_p⟦t_1, …, t_n⟧ and Spf of every complete regular local ring are regular; so is the p-adic completion of a smooth ℤ_p-scheme.
Spf k⟦x, y⟧/(xy) is Cohen–Macaulay but not regular.

nodes.title: Codimension formula on Cohen–Macaulay formal schemes
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian formal scheme all of whose stalks are Cohen–Macaulay (for instance a regular one), and Z ⊆ X a nonempty closed formal subscheme. (a) The infimum defining codim_X Z is attained at a closed point, and on every affine formal open Spf A meeting Z, with Z ∩ Spf A = Spf(A/𝔞), codim_{Spf A}(Z ∩ Spf A) = height(𝔞) := min over the minimal primes q of 𝔞 of ht q, the codimension of V(𝔞) in Spec A. (b) If moreover X has pure dimension d, then codim_X Z = d − dim Z.
hypotheses: X is noetherian, so every point has a closed specialisation in X. The affine height identity also applies on each affine formal open of a locally noetherian X.
All stalks Cohen–Macaulay (catenary and equidimensional).
(b) only: pure dimension d, i.e. dim O_{X,x} = d at every closed point.
proofSteps: For a Cohen–Macaulay local ring R and a prime P, dim R = dim R_P + dim R/P (Stacks 00NA); hence for an ideal 𝔞 of R, dim R − dim R/𝔞 = min over minimal primes of ht P = ht 𝔞.

On Spf A, replace stalks by localisations A_p (FK.0/stalk-completion-comparison): codim_z(Z, X) = dim A_p − dim (A/𝔞)_p = min over the minimal primes of 𝔞 contained in p of their heights. For a generalisation p′ ⊆ p this minimum runs over a subset, so local codimension does not decrease under generalisation and the local infimum is attained at the maximal ideals. On noetherian X every point has a globally closed specialisation, giving the global assertion too.
Every minimal prime of 𝔞 lies in a maximal ideal, and all maximal ideals are closed points of Spf A, so the infimum over maximal ideals is min ht q = height(𝔞): this is (a).
(b) At a closed point z, codim_z(Z, X) = d − dim O_{Z,z}; the infimum over closed points is d − sup_z dim O_{Z,z} = d − dim Z, dimensions of stalks increasing under specialisation.
acceptance: Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧ (d = 2): Z = V(t) has dim 1 and codim 1; Z = V(p, t) has dim 0 and codim 2.

The height description fails without the Cohen–Macaulay hypothesis: in Spf k⟦x, y, z⟧/(xz, yz) (a plane union a line through the origin, not equidimensional) the line V(x, y) is an irreducible component, of height 0 in the coordinate ring, while dim O_{X,x} − dim O_{L,x} = 2 − 1 = 1 at the closed point.

sources.match: In a Cohen–Macaulay local ring, dim R = dim R_p + dim R/p for every prime p.
The filtration comparison F^{d−i}K_0^Y(X) ≅ F_iK′_0(Y) for regular X of pure dimension d needs codim_X Z ≥ d − i exactly when dim Z ≤ i, which is this formula.

nodes.title: Regular immersions and effective Cartier divisors of formal schemes
nodes.statement: A closed immersion i : Z → X of locally noetherian formal schemes with coherent ideal 𝒜 ⊆ O_X is a regular immersion if for every z ∈ |Z| the ideal 𝒜_z ⊆ O_{X,z} is generated by a regular sequence (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular) f_1, …, f_m of O_{X,z}; m = codim_z(Z, X) is then locally constant on |Z|. An effective Cartier divisor is a closed formal subscheme D whose ideal is invertible (locally generated by one nonzerodivisor), i.e. a regular immersion of codimension 1. On Spf A with Z = Spf(A/𝔞), i is a regular immersion iff 𝔞 is locally on Spec A near every maximal ideal generated by a regular sequence; if X and Z are both regular, every closed immersion Z → X is a regular immersion.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian.
The local equations are taken in the formal stalks O_{X,z}; by faithful flatness of A_p → O_{X,z} (FK.0/stalk-completion-comparison) this is equivalent to the condition in A_p.
proofSteps: A regular sequence in the noetherian local ring O_{X,z} drops the dimension by exactly one at each step (Stacks 00KW), so m = dim O_{X,z} − dim O_{Z,z} = codim_z(Z, X).
Regularity of a sequence descends and ascends along the faithfully flat local maps A_p → O_{X,z} (Koszul homology commutes with flat base change and is detected faithfully).
If O_{X,z} and O_{Z,z} = O_{X,z}/𝒜_z are regular local, 𝒜_z is generated by part of a regular system of parameters, which is a regular sequence.
The Koszul complex of a regular sequence is a resolution of the quotient (Stacks 062F; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/koszul-complex), so O_Z has a local finite free resolution of length m.
acceptance: V(t − p) ⊂ Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧ is an effective Cartier divisor isomorphic to Spf ℤ_p.
The closed point of Spf k⟦x, y⟧/(xy) is not a regular immersion: the ring has depth 1, so its maximal ideal contains no regular sequence of length 2 = number of generators.

sources.locator: Lemma B.2 and its proof, pp. 974–975
sources.match: The closed immersion Z_1 → X is assumed to be a regular immersion (for example X and Z_1 regular), so Z_1 is cut out at each point of Z_1 ∩ Z_2 by a regular sequence of the local ring of X, whose Koszul complex is a free resolution.

A closed formal subscheme is a Cartier divisor if its ideal sheaf is invertible; Kudla–Rapoport divisors are Cartier divisors and their pullbacks along maps with injective local homomorphisms between regular formal schemes stay Cartier.
A nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal drops the dimension by one; a regular sequence is Koszul-regular.

nodes.title: Formal support of a coherent module
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme, Y ⊆ X the closed formal subscheme with coherent ideal 𝒥 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme). A coherent O_X-module F is formally supported on Y if every point of |X| has an open neighbourhood U with 𝒥^n·F|_U = 0 for some n; on noetherian X one n works globally. Coh_Y(X) ⊆ Coh(X) is the full subcategory of such F; it is a Serre subcategory. On X = Spf A with Y = Spf(A/J) and F = M^Δ (M a finite A-module): F is formally supported on Y iff J^nM = 0 for some n iff Supp_A(M) ⊆ V(J) ⊆ Spec A. Formal support depends on 𝒥 only through its radical, and it is not detected by the topological support Supp F ⊆ |X|.
hypotheses: X locally noetherian; 𝒥 a coherent ideal.
Supports are formal (power of the ideal kills), not topological.
proofSteps: Extension closure: if 𝒥^aF′ = 0 and 𝒥^bF″ = 0 for 0 → F′ → F → F″ → 0 then 𝒥^{a+b}F = 0; subobjects and quotients are clear, and coherence is stable (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module-properties).

Affine case: Γ(Spf A, ·) is an equivalence between Coh(Spf A) and finite A-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence), and for a finite module over a noetherian ring, J^nM = 0 for some n iff Supp M ⊆ V(J) (Stacks 00L6).
Radical: if √𝒥 = √𝒥′ then each contains a power of the other on quasi-compact opens.
For F formally supported on Y and G on Z, F ⊗ G and Tor sheaves are killed by 𝒥_Y^a + 𝒥_Z^b ⊇ (𝒥_Y + 𝒥_Z)^{a+b−1}, i.e. formally supported on Y ∩ Z := V(𝒥_Y + 𝒥_Z).
acceptance: On Spf ℤ_p with Y = V(p) = Spec F_p, O itself has topological support all of |Spf ℤ_p| = |Y| but is not p-power torsion, so it is not formally supported on Y.
(A/J^n)^Δ is formally supported on V(J) for every n.

nodes.title: Tor sheaves of coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme
nodes.statement: For a locally noetherian formal scheme X and coherent O_X-modules F, G, there are coherent O_X-modules Tor_j^{O_X}(F, G), j ≥ 0, with Tor_0 = F ⊗ G, such that on every affine formal open Spf A with F = M^Δ, G = N^Δ one has Tor_j|_{Spf A} ≅ Tor_j^A(M, N)^Δ, compatibly with restriction to smaller affine formal opens; their stalks are Tor_j^{O_{X,x}}(F_x, G_x). They are symmetric in F and G, give long exact sequences in each variable, are formally supported on Y ∩ Z when F is formally supported on Y and G on Z, vanish for j > d when every stalk has global dimension ≤ d (for instance X regular of dimension d), and vanish for j > 0 when F is locally free. When the pair has a uniform finite Tor bound (for example X regular of finite dimension, or one input perfect), the derived tensor class is [F ⊗^L G] := Σ_j (−1)^j [Tor_j^{O_X}(F, G)].
hypotheses: X locally noetherian; F, G coherent.
Tor is taken over O_X itself, never over a thickening X_n = V(𝒥^{n+1}) or over the reduction.

Each Tor_j exists without finite amplitude. An alternating class is defined only when all sufficiently high Tor_j vanish uniformly; for locally noetherian exhaustion constructions this bound may instead be checked on each noetherian member.
proofSteps: Affine definition: Tor_j^A(M, N) is a finite A-module (A noetherian), so (·)^Δ gives a coherent module on Spf A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/associated-formal-module).

Compatibility: for f ∈ A the completed localisation A_{f} is flat over A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization), so Tor_j^A(M, N) ⊗_A A_{f} ≅ Tor_j^{A_{f}}(M_{f}, N_{f}), matching the restriction of (·)^Δ; glue over an affine formal cover (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing).
Stalks: A → O_{X,x} is flat (FK.0/stalk-completion-comparison), so Tor commutes with passing to the stalk.

Long exact sequences and symmetry from the module statements (Stacks 00M0, 00M3); support from FK.0/formal-support; vanishing above d from Stacks 00O7 applied stalkwise, a coherent sheaf with zero stalks being zero.
acceptance: On Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧: Tor_1(O/(t), O/(t)) ≅ O/(t) and Tor_1(O/(t), O/(t − p)) = 0.
Computing over the reduction gives the wrong answer: Tor_1^{F_p}(F_p, F_p) = 0, while Tor_1^{ℤ_p}(F_p, F_p) ≅ F_p on Spf ℤ_p.

nodes.title: The Grothendieck group K′₀ of coherent modules on a noetherian formal scheme
nodes.statement: For a noetherian formal scheme X, K′_0(X) := AbelianK0(Coh X) (TauCeti.AbelianK0), the free abelian group on isomorphism classes of coherent O_X-modules modulo [F] = [F′] + [F″] for every short exact sequence 0 → F′ → F → F″ → 0; K′_0(X)_ℚ := K′_0(X) ⊗ ℚ. It is functorial for restriction to open formal subschemes, for pushforward along closed immersions (i_* is exact), and for pullback along flat morphisms. For X = Spf A, Γ(X, ·) gives K′_0(Spf A) ≅ G_0(A) := ExactK0(finiteModulesExactStructure A) (TauCeti); for a noetherian scheme regarded as a formal scheme, K′_0 is π_0 of the parent's G-theory (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.2/g-theory-of-a-scheme).
hypotheses: X noetherian (quasi-compact and locally noetherian), so Coh X is an essentially small abelian category (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module-properties): finitely many affine formal opens, finite modules and gluing data.
Integral coefficients; rational coefficients only by explicit tensoring.
proofSteps: Coh X is abelian (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module-properties) and essentially small, so TauCeti.AbelianK0 applies.
Exact functors induce maps on AbelianK0: restriction to opens, i_* for closed immersions, f^* for flat f (flatness of the stalk maps makes f^* exact on coherent modules).
On Spf A the equivalence Coh(Spf A) ≃ finite A-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence) is exact, so it identifies the abelian K_0 with TauCeti's G_0 of finite modules.
For a noetherian scheme the coherent categories agree (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module, compatibility with ofScheme) and the parent identifies G_0 with π_0 G.
acceptance: K′_0(Spf ℤ_p) ≅ ℤ via generic rank, with [F_p] = 0 (from 0 → ℤ_p → ℤ_p → F_p → 0).
K′_0(Spf k⟦x, y⟧/(xy)) ≅ ℤ², detected by the ranks at the two minimal primes; [k] = 0.

nodes.title: Dévissage for formally supported coherent modules
nodes.statement: Let X be a noetherian formal scheme and Y = V(𝒥) a closed formal subscheme. Pushforward along i : Y → X induces an isomorphism K′_0(Y) ≅ K_0(Coh_Y(X)) (abelian K_0 of the Serre subcategory of FK.0/formal-support). Hence K′_0(V(𝒥^n)) ≅ K′_0(Y) for every n ≥ 1, and K′_0(Y) depends only on the radical of 𝒥; every coherent F formally supported on Y has a class [F] ∈ K′_0(Y).
hypotheses: X noetherian, so a single power of 𝒥 kills each object of Coh_Y(X).
proofSteps: Each F in Coh_Y(X) has the finite filtration F ⊇ 𝒥F ⊇ 𝒥²F ⊇ ⋯ ⊇ 𝒥^nF = 0 whose quotients are killed by 𝒥, i.e. are pushforwards of coherent O_Y-modules.

Quillen's dévissage theorem (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.3/devissage-theorem; in degree 0 the inverse is F ↦ Σ_k [𝒥^kF/𝒥^{k+1}F], independent of the filtration by Schreier refinement) gives the isomorphism.
Applying it to Y and to V(𝒥^n), which have the same formally supported objects, gives K′_0(V(𝒥^n)) ≅ K′_0(Y); the radical statement follows from FK.0/formal-support.
acceptance: For Y = V(p) ⊂ Spf ℤ_p, K′_0(Spec F_p) ≅ ℤ ≅ K_0(Coh_Y(Spf ℤ_p)), generated by [F_p], and [ℤ/p^n] = n[F_p].

sources.match: The homology of a supported complex is regarded as an element of K′_0(Y), and O_Y ⊗^L O_Z is viewed in K′_0(Y ∩ Z) ≃ K_0^{Y∩Z}(X), which uses that formally supported coherent modules have classes in K′_0 of the support.
On a noetherian ring a power of the ideal kills every finite module supported in V(I), which makes the 𝒥-adic filtration finite.

nodes.title: Strict complexes with formal support
nodes.statement: For a noetherian formal scheme X and a closed formal subscheme Y, C^b_Y(X) is the category of bounded chain complexes of locally free coherent O_X-modules of finite rank whose homology sheaves are formally supported on Y (FK.0/formal-support), with chain maps as morphisms. It is closed under shifts, mapping cones, finite direct sums and degreewise split extensions; E ⊗ F ∈ C^b_{Y∩Z}(X) for E ∈ C^b_Y(X), F ∈ C^b_Z(X); and for any morphism g : X′ → X of noetherian formal schemes, g^*E ∈ C^b_{g^{-1}Y}(X′) with g^{-1}Y := V(g^*𝒥·O_{X′}). On X = Spf A, Γ identifies C^b_{Spf(A/J)}(Spf A) with the bounded complexes of finite projective A-modules whose homology is supported in V(J) ⊆ Spec A, i.e. with Gillet–Soulé's strict category of Spec A with support V(J).
hypotheses: Global strict complexes: a perfect complex need not be quasi-isomorphic to one of these unless X has the resolution property (FK.2/regular-supported-comparison).
Support is formal: acyclicity 'outside Y' means homology killed by a power of the ideal of Y.
proofSteps: Homology of a cone and of a degreewise split extension sits in long exact sequences, and Coh_Y(X) is a Serre subcategory.

Tensor product: on Spf A, E ⊗ F is a bounded complex of finite projectives; its homology is supported in V(J_Y) ∩ V(J_Z) because E is exact after localising at any prime outside V(J_Y), hence so is E ⊗ F (Künneth over a localisation where E is contractible).

Pullback: on affine charts A → A′, a bounded complex of finite projectives exact at all primes outside V(J) stays exact at all primes of A′ outside V(JA′), since such a prime lies over a prime outside V(J) and localisations commute with base change; the homology of E ⊗_A A′ is then supported in V(JA′) (Stacks 00L6).
Locally free coherent modules on Spf A are the M^Δ with M finite projective (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence and local freeness at every maximal ideal).
acceptance: On Spf ℤ_p the Koszul complex [O →p O] lies in C^b_{V(p)}(Spf ℤ_p); [O →0 O] does not, its homology O being supported on |V(p)| only topologically.

nodes.title: The Gillet–Soulé group K₀^Y of a noetherian formal scheme
nodes.statement: For a noetherian formal scheme X and a closed formal subscheme Y, K_0^Y(X) is the free abelian group on isomorphism classes of objects of C^b_Y(X) (FK.1/strict-supported-complexes) modulo [E] = [E′] + [E″] for every degreewise exact sequence 0 → E′ → E → E″ → 0 in C^b_Y(X), and [E] = [F] whenever E and F are quasi-isomorphic by a chain map. K_0(X) := K_0^X(X). Consequences: exact complexes have class 0, [E[1]] = −[E], and [cone(u)] = [F] − [E] for u : E → F. Maps: support enlargement K_0^Y(X) → K_0^{Y′}(X) for Y ⊆ Y′; restriction to open formal subschemes; pullback g^* : K_0^Y(X) → K_0^{g⁻¹Y}(X′) for every morphism g of noetherian formal schemes. K_0(X) is a commutative ring and K_0^Y(X) a K_0(X)-module under the cup product (FK.1/supported-cup-product). This is not the exact K_0 of the category of complexes: the quasi-isomorphism relation is essential.
hypotheses: X noetherian; Y closed formal subscheme.
Global strict model; without the resolution property it may differ from a K_0 of locally perfect complexes, and nothing here asserts otherwise.
proofSteps: The relations are compatible with ⊗, pullback and support enlargement because these preserve degreewise exact sequences and quasi-isomorphisms of complexes of locally free modules.
An exact complex E is quasi-isomorphic to 0; [E[1]] + [E] = [cone(id_E)] = 0 from the degreewise split sequence E → cone(id_E) → E[1].

On Spf A the group is Gillet–Soulé's K_0^{V(J)}(Spec A) (FK.1/affine-transport), which the parent identifies with Thomason–Trobaugh's K_0(Spec A on V(J)) (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.6/gillet-soule-strict-support-comparison).
acceptance: For A local, K_0(Spf A) ≅ ℤ by rank, every finite projective A-module being free.

nodes.title: Affine transport: K-groups of Spf A are those of Spec A
nodes.statement: Let A be a noetherian adic ring, J ⊆ A an ideal, X = Spf A and Y = Spf(A/J). (i) Γ(X, ·) is an equivalence from C^b_Y(X) onto the category of bounded complexes of finite projective A-modules with homology supported in V(J), compatible with ⊗, shifts, cones and quasi-isomorphisms. (ii) Hence K_0^Y(Spf A) ≅ K_0^{V(J)}(Spec A) in Gillet–Soulé's strict model, compatibly with cup products, support enlargement and pullback along continuous maps A → A′. (iii) K′_0(Spf(A/J)) ≅ G_0(A/J) ≅ G_0(Spec(A/J)). (iv) If A is regular of finite Krull dimension, closed formal subschemes Spf(A/𝔞) ⊆ Spf A and closed subschemes V(𝔞) ⊆ Spec A have the same codimension (FK.0/formal-codimension-formula), so the codimension filtrations correspond. Every statement the parent proves for the affine scheme Spec A of a noetherian regular ring of finite dimension therefore holds for Spf A.
hypotheses: A noetherian adic; Spec A is affine, hence separated and has the resolution property.
No such transport is asserted for non-affine formal schemes.
proofSteps: Coherent modules on Spf A are finite A-modules and locally free ones are finite projective (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence); homology commutes with Γ by exactness.
Formal support of M^Δ on V(J) is Supp M ⊆ V(J) (FK.0/formal-support), the support condition of Gillet–Soulé's strict model on Spec A.
The two presentations have the same generators and relations, so the groups coincide; products and maps are defined by the same formulas.
Codimension: FK.0/formal-codimension-formula on Spf A and the height description on Spec A.
acceptance: For A = ℤ_p⟦t⟧ and J = (p, t): K_0^{V(p,t)}(Spf A) ≅ K_0^{V(p,t)}(Spec A) ≅ ℤ, generated by the Koszul complex of (p, t).

nodes.title: The supported cup product
nodes.statement: For a noetherian formal scheme X and closed formal subschemes Y, Z, the tensor product of complexes induces a biadditive map ∪ : K_0^Y(X) × K_0^Z(X) → K_0^{Y∩Z}(X), [E] ∪ [F] = [Tot(E ⊗ F)], where Y ∩ Z := V(𝒥_Y + 𝒥_Z). It is associative, graded-commutative (commutative on these K_0's), unital with unit [O_X] ∈ K_0(X), compatible with support enlargement and restriction, and with pullback: g^*(a ∪ b) = g^*a ∪ g^*b. On Spf A it is the Gillet–Soulé product of Spec A with supports.

The product is derived: its homology is computed by Tor, not by tensoring homology.

nodes.title: The Tor pairing and derived intersections on a regular formal scheme
nodes.statement: Let X be a regular noetherian formal scheme of finite dimension. For closed formal subschemes Y, Z there is a biadditive pairing K′_0(Y) × K′_0(Z) → K′_0(Y ∩ Z), [F] ·^L [G] := Σ_j (−1)^j [Tor_j^{O_X}(i_*F, i_*G)] (FK.0/formal-tor-sheaves; finite since Tor_j = 0 for j > dim X), symmetric, associative and unital with unit [O_X], compatible with pushforward along closed immersions Y ⊆ Y′. The derived intersection is Y ∩^L_X Z := [O_Y] ·^L [O_Z] ∈ K′_0(Y ∩ Z). It is compatible with the cup product: h_{Y∩Z}(a ∪ b) = h_Y(a) ·^L h_Z(b) for a ∈ K_0^Y(X), b ∈ K_0^Z(X). On a regular noetherian scheme it is the parent's K-module pairing on G_0 (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.2/tensor-product-pairings).
hypotheses: X regular (finite Tor-dimension of every stalk) and noetherian of finite dimension.
Without regularity the alternating sum need not be finite and the pairing is not defined.
proofSteps: Bilinearity: a short exact sequence in either variable gives the long exact Tor sequence, which is finite, and its alternating sum vanishes in K_0(Coh_{Y∩Z}(X)) ≅ K′_0(Y ∩ Z) (FK.1/formal-supported-devissage).

Use the ordinary homotopy-category shadow of EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/presentability-and-derived-tensor on the ringed space (|X|, O_X). Truncation triangles give finite global hyper-Tor spectral sequences of coherent sheaves for the two bracketings of F ⊗^L G ⊗^L H. Their Euler classes agree with the iterated pairings by dévissage, and derived associativity identifies the abutments. Equality of K′_0 classes is obtained globally; K′_0 classes are not detected by stalks or by an affine cover.

For strict E and F, filter the global derived tensor by their bounded homology truncations. The finite hyper-Tor spectral sequences have terms Tor_p(H_q(E), H_r(F)) and abutment H_*(E ⊗ F); their Euler classes in the supported coherent category give homologyClass_cup. Finite dimension bounds Tor uniformly.
Scheme case: Tor sheaves agree (FK.0/formal-tor-sheaves) and the parent's pairing is [E ⊗^L F] on K_0 × G_0.
acceptance: On Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧: V(t) ∩^L V(t − p) = [Spec F_p] = 1 and V(t) ∩^L V(t) = [O_{V(t)}] − [O_{V(t)}] = 0 in K′_0(V(t)) ≅ ℤ.

nodes.title: Regular supported dévissage: K₀^Y(X) ≅ K′₀(Y)
nodes.statement: Let X be a regular noetherian formal scheme of finite dimension d with the resolution property: every coherent O_X-module is a quotient of a locally free coherent one (automatic for X = Spf A). Then for every closed formal subscheme Y ⊆ X the homology class map h_Y : K_0^Y(X) → K′_0(Y) (FK.1/homology-class-map) is an isomorphism. Its inverse sends [F], for F ∈ Coh_Y(X), to the class of any finite resolution E → F by locally free coherent modules (of length ≤ d), which lies in C^b_Y(X). Consequently K_0^Y(X) is identified with K′_0(Y), K_0(X) ≅ K′_0(X), and for an open U ⊆ X containing Y and also having the resolution property, the restriction K_0^Y(X) → K_0^Y(U) is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: X regular of finite Krull dimension d, noetherian.
Resolution property for X (for example X affine). Without it the theorem is not asserted; a locally perfect model of K-theory would be needed.
The statement is false without regularity (FK.1/homology-class-map, node non-example).
proofSteps: Existence of resolutions: by the resolution property choose locally free E_0 → F surjective, then E_1 → ker, and so on; the d-th syzygy has stalks of projective dimension 0, since regular local rings of dimension ≤ d have global dimension ≤ d (Stacks 00O7), hence is locally free (a coherent module with free stalks is locally free: on Spf A a finite module free at every maximal ideal is projective).

Use finite resolutions of bounded coherent complexes and of finite diagrams, constructed by successive epimorphisms from locally free sheaves onto the required fibre products. Common refinements and mapping cones compare resolutions and give additivity, using the resolving-subcategory argument (GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.3/resolution-theorem; GrothendieckEulerForms Layer 3). Vector bundles are closed under extensions and kernels of epimorphisms between vector bundles locally, but need not be projective objects of Coh X; do not invoke a projective horseshoe lemma or assume arbitrary lifts to preselected resolutions.

Apply that bounded-complex resolution argument with the quasi-isomorphisms whose homology is formally supported on Y. It compares the strict presentation with the bounded coherent derived category supported on Y. Bounded truncations identify its K_0 with K_0(Coh_Y(X)); dévissage then gives K′_0(Y). On a coherent sheaf h of any chosen resolution is its class, and the truncation Euler identity proves the reverse composite for every strict complex.

On X = Spf A this is the parent's comparison for the affine regular scheme Spec A transported by FK.1/affine-transport (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.6/gillet-soule-strict-support-comparison together with SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.3/regular-support-devissage).
Restriction: h commutes with restriction to U, and K′_0(Y) is the same whether computed in X or in U ⊇ Y; apply the theorem to X and to U.
acceptance: X = Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧, Y = V(p, t): K_0^Y(X) ≅ K′_0(Spec F_p) ≅ ℤ, generated by the Koszul complex of (p, t).

nodes.title: K-groups of locally noetherian formal schemes by noetherian exhaustion
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme which is the increasing union of a directed family (X_i)_{i∈I} of noetherian open formal subschemes. Define K′_0(X) := lim_i K′_0(X_i), K_0(X) := lim_i K_0(X_i) and, for a closed formal subscheme Y with Y_i := Y ∩ X_i, K_0^Y(X) := lim_i K_0^{Y_i}(X_i), along restriction maps; F^jK_0^Y(X) := lim_i F^jK_0^{Y_i}(X_i) ⊆ K_0^Y(X) and F_jK′_0(X) likewise, with Gr^j := F^j/F^{j+1} of these limits. Cup products, homology class maps, pullbacks along morphisms compatible with exhaustions, and Tor pairings (on regular members of finite dimension) pass to the limit. The groups do not depend on the exhaustion: they are canonically the limits over all quasi-compact open formal subschemes. If Y is quasi-compact, Y ⊆ X_{i_0}, and all X_i are regular of finite dimension with the resolution property, then K_0^Y(X) ≅ K_0^Y(X_{i_0}) ≅ K′_0(Y).
hypotheses: X locally noetherian and exhausted by noetherian opens (for instance any locally noetherian formal scheme whose underlying space is a countable increasing union of quasi-compact opens).
These are limits over open subschemes, not over the thickenings X_n of an ideal of definition; they are not continuous K-theory of thickenings (RefinedTraceMethodsPartII's concern).
Gr^j of the limits is not asserted to be the limit of the Gr^j.
proofSteps: Restriction maps are compatible with composition, so the inverse systems are defined; all structure maps commute with restriction.
Independence: a quasi-compact open lies in finitely many X_i, hence in one by directedness; so each exhaustion is cofinal in the poset of quasi-compact opens, and the limits agree canonically.
Stabilisation: for i ≥ i_0 the restriction K_0^Y(X_i) → K_0^Y(X_{i_0}) is an isomorphism by FK.2/regular-supported-comparison (both are K′_0(Y)), so the system is eventually constant.
The closed-union decomposition of FK.3/closed-union-decomposition passes to the limit of the noetherian isomorphisms, but not to cokernels of limits (lim¹ terms; PAPER-ZHANG-21/E60).
acceptance: For X = ⊔_{n∈ℕ} Spf ℤ_p, exhausted by finite unions, K′_0(X) ≅ ∏_n ℤ.
For X noetherian, the one-member exhaustion recovers the noetherian groups.

nodes.title: Closed-union decomposition of K′₀ modulo the overlap (Lemma B.1)
nodes.statement: (a) Let X be a noetherian formal scheme and X = X_1 ∪ X_2 a union of closed formal subschemes X_k = V(𝒥_k) with 𝒥_1 ∩ 𝒥_2 = 0; put X_12 := V(𝒥_1 + 𝒥_2). For coherent E on X the sheaves Tor_1^{O_X}(E, O_{X_k}) and E ⊗ O_{X_12} are formally supported on X_12, and [E] ↦ ([E ⊗ O_{X_1}], [E ⊗ O_{X_2}]) induces an isomorphism coker(K′_0(X_12) → K′_0(X)) ≅ coker(K′_0(X_12) → K′_0(X_1)) ⊕ coker(K′_0(X_12) → K′_0(X_2)), whose inverse is induced by (a_1, a_2) ↦ i_{1*}a_1 + i_{2*}a_2. The maps K′_0(X_12) → K′_0(X_k) need not be injective; the quotients are cokernels. (b) If X is locally noetherian with a noetherian exhaustion (X_i), the isomorphisms of (a) for the X_i form an isomorphism of inverse systems, giving lim_i coker_i(X) ≅ lim_i coker_i(X_1) ⊕ lim_i coker_i(X_2); the comparison of the cokernel of a limit with the limit of cokernels is not asserted.
hypotheses: (a) X noetherian; 𝒥_1 ∩ 𝒥_2 = 0 (scheme-theoretic union).

(b) Cokernels of inverse limits may differ from inverse limits of cokernels by lim¹ terms (PAPER-ZHANG-21/E60); the paper's one-line reduction to the noetherian case is replaced by the statement about limits of cokernels.
proofSteps: Well-definedness: E ↦ E ⊗ O_{X_1} is right exact, and for 0 → E′ → E → E″ → 0 the defect is the image of Tor_1(E″, O_{X_1}). On an affine formal open Spf A, after localising at a prime q of A not containing 𝔧_1 + 𝔧_2, one of 𝔧_1, 𝔧_2 becomes the unit ideal and the other zero (their product lies in 𝔧_1 ∩ 𝔧_2 = 0), so O_{X_1} is a direct factor of O_X there and Tor_1 vanishes; hence Tor_1 is supported in V(𝔧_1 + 𝔧_2) ⊆ Spec A and formally supported on X_12 (FK.0/formal-support). The localisation is at primes of the coordinate ring, not at points of |X|, which may all lie in |X_12|.
Classes of modules formally supported on X_12 lie in the image of K′_0(X_12) (FK.1/formal-supported-devissage), so the map is well defined on cokernels.

Tensor the exact sequence 0 → O_X/(𝒥_1 ∩ 𝒥_2) → O_X/𝒥_1 ⊕ O_X/𝒥_2 → O_X/(𝒥_1 + 𝒥_2) → 0 with E: the four-term sequence Tor_1(E, O_{X_12}) → E → (E ⊗ O_{X_1}) ⊕ (E ⊗ O_{X_2}) → E ⊗ O_{X_12} → 0 shows i_{1*}[E ⊗ O_{X_1}] + i_{2*}[E ⊗ O_{X_2}] = [E] modulo K′_0(X_12).
Conversely for an O_{X_1}-module F, F ⊗ O_{X_1} = F and F ⊗ O_{X_2} = F/𝒥_2F is an O_{X_12}-module, so the other composite is the identity.
(b): restriction maps commute with all maps in (a); finite direct sums commute with inverse limits.
acceptance: X = Spf k⟦x, y⟧/(xy) = V(x) ∪ V(y), X_12 = Spec k: K′_0(X_12) ≅ ℤ maps to 0 in K′_0(V(x)) ≅ K′_0(Spf k⟦y⟧) ≅ ℤ (since [k] = 0 there), so the overlap map is not injective; both sides of (a) are ℤ ⊕ ℤ, matching K′_0(X) ≅ ℤ² with [k] = 0.
If X_1 ∩ X_2 = ∅, (a) is the additivity K′_0(X_1 ⊔ X_2) ≅ K′_0(X_1) ⊕ K′_0(X_2).

nodes.title: Tor vanishing in the expected dimension (Lemma B.2(i))
nodes.statement: Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme, Z_1 → X a regular immersion (FK.0/formal-regular-immersion) and Z_2 ⊆ X a Cohen–Macaulay closed formal subscheme. Suppose that at every point z ∈ |Z_1 ∩ Z_2|, codim_z(Z_1 ∩ Z_2, X) = codim_z(Z_1, X) + codim_z(Z_2, X). Then Tor_i^{O_X}(O_{Z_1}, O_{Z_2}) = 0 for all i > 0, so on every noetherian open the finite Tor class satisfies O_{Z_1} ⊗^L O_{Z_2} = O_{Z_1} ⊗ O_{Z_2} = O_{Z_1∩Z_2} in K′_0(Z_1 ∩ Z_2), and Z_1 ∩ Z_2 → Z_2 is again a regular immersion.
hypotheses: Z_1 → X regular immersion, for example X and Z_1 regular.
Z_2 Cohen–Macaulay; the conclusion fails without it.
Codimensions are those of FK.0/formal-local-dimension; pure-dimensionality, assumed in the source, is not needed for this part.
proofSteps: Stalks: Tor sheaves are computed on stalks (FK.0/formal-tor-sheaves), and a coherent sheaf with zero stalks at all points of |X| is zero; away from |Z_1 ∩ Z_2| some argument is killed by a unit.

At z with R = O_{X,z}, the ideal of Z_1 is generated by a regular sequence f_1, …, f_m (m = codim_z(Z_1, X)), whose Koszul complex K(f) is a free resolution of O_{Z_1,z} (Stacks 062F; EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/koszul-complex). Hence Tor_i^R(O_{Z_1,z}, O_{Z_2,z}) = H_i(K(f̄; O_{Z_2,z})).

The hypothesis says dim O_{Z_2,z}/(f̄) = dim O_{Z_2,z} − m; in the Cohen–Macaulay local ring O_{Z_2,z} this means f̄ is a regular sequence (Stacks 02JN), so its Koszul complex is exact in positive degrees.
H_0 = O_{Z_2,z}/(f̄) = O_{Z_1∩Z_2,z}, and f̄ regular gives the last claim.

On each noetherian open the locally constant regular-immersion ranks have a finite upper bound, so the Tor Euler class is a finite sum there. For non-quasi-compact X take the inverse-limit class, rather than an unbounded global sum.
acceptance: On Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧: Z_1 = V(t), Z_2 = V(t − p) meet in Spec F_p of the expected codimension 2, and Tor_1 = 0.

Serre's example: in Spf k⟦x, y, z, w⟧ let Z_2 = V(x, y) ∪ V(z, w) (not Cohen–Macaulay) and Z_1 = V(x − z, y − w). The intersection is the closed point, of the expected codimension 4, but O_{Z_1∩Z_2} = k⟦x, y⟧/(x², xy, y²) has length 3 while the Euler characteristic is 2, so Tor_1 ≠ 0.

sources.locator: Lemma B.2(i) and its proof, pp. 974–975
sources.match: With Z_1 → X a regular immersion and Z_2 Cohen–Macaulay, expected codimension at every point of Z_1 ∩ Z_2 forces the higher Tor sheaves to vanish: the Koszul complex of the local equations of Z_1 stays a resolution after restriction to Z_2.
Applied with the graph Γ_g′ and N_{n−1} × N_{n−1}, local complete intersections in N_n × N_n meeting in the expected dimension, to get vanishing of higher Tor.
Regular sequences are Koszul-regular; in a Cohen–Macaulay local ring a sequence in the maximal ideal is regular exactly when it cuts the dimension by its length.

nodes.title: Tor vanishing on an expected-dimensional part (Lemma B.2(ii))
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of FK.3/expected-dimension-tor-vanishing except the dimension condition, let X be noetherian and Z_1 ∩ Z_2 = Y ∪ Y′ (𝒥_Y ∩ 𝒥_{Y′} = 𝒥_{Z_1∩Z_2}) with Y of the expected dimension: codim_z(Y, X) = codim_z(Z_1, X) + codim_z(Z_2, X) at every z ∈ |Y|. Then for every i > 0 the restriction Tor_i^{O_X}(O_{Z_1}, O_{Z_2}) ⊗ O_Y is formally supported on Y ∩ Y′, so its class lies in the image of K′_0(Y ∩ Y′) → K′_0(Y); equivalently, under FK.3/closed-union-decomposition the Y-component of [Tor_i] vanishes in coker(K′_0(Y ∩ Y′) → K′_0(Y)). Hence the Y-component of O_{Z_1} ⊗^L O_{Z_2} is the class of O_Y modulo the image of K′_0(Y ∩ Y′). The sheaf Tor_i ⊗ O_Y itself need not vanish.
hypotheses: Z_1 → X regular immersion, Z_2 Cohen–Macaulay, X noetherian (for the locally noetherian case use FK.2/noetherian-exhaustion-k-groups).
The localisation away from Y′ must be done at primes of the stalks O_{Z_2,z}, not at points of |X|: in Spf ℤ_p⟦s, t⟧, Y = V(s, t) and Y′ = V(s, t − p) have the same underlying point.
This expands the compressed proof of the source; review rejects E1 as an allegation of a source mistake, since the printed argument never restricts localisation to topological points.
proofSteps: Fix z ∈ |Y| and work in the Cohen–Macaulay local ring B = O_{Z_2,z}, where Z_1 is cut out by f̄_1, …, f̄_m and Tor_i ⊗ O_Y is a finite B-module.

Let P be a prime of B in V(I_Y) not containing I_{Y′}. Near P, Z_1 ∩ Z_2 = Y. By Krull's height theorem (Stacks 0BBZ) every minimal prime of (f̄) has height ≤ m, so every component of Y through P has dimension ≥ dim B − m; with the expected dimension at z (Stacks 00NA, B Cohen–Macaulay) every such component has dimension exactly dim B − m, hence dim B_P/(f̄) = dim B_P − m.
So f̄ is a regular sequence in the Cohen–Macaulay local ring B_P (Stacks 02JN) and the Koszul homology H_i(K(f̄; B))_P = 0 for i > 0.

Thus Supp_B(Tor_i ⊗ O_Y) ⊆ V(I_Y + I_{Y′}); being finite, it is killed by a power of that ideal (Stacks 00L6), i.e. formally supported on Y ∩ Y′, and FK.1/formal-supported-devissage puts its class in the image of K′_0(Y ∩ Y′).
The last claim follows from the long exact sequences and FK.3/closed-union-decomposition.
acceptance: If Y′ = ∅ the statement is FK.3/expected-dimension-tor-vanishing.

Consumer pattern: for the Kudla–Rapoport cycle of a rank n−1 lattice, Z(L♭) = Z(L♭)_H ∪ Z(L♭)_V with the horizontal part of expected dimension, so the horizontal component of the derived cycle in Gr^{n−1} is represented by the structure sheaf of Z(L♭)_H (Li–Zhang, Definition 5.2.1).

sources.locator: Lemma B.2(ii) and its proof, pp. 974–975
sources.match: If the intersection is a union of Y and Y′ with Y of the expected dimension, the higher Tor sheaves restricted to Y vanish modulo K′_0(Y ∩ Y′); the paper says this is proved like (i) by combining with Lemma B.1.
The horizontal part of the derived Kudla–Rapoport cycle has the expected dimension and is represented by its structure sheaf by Lemma B.2(ii).
Krull's height theorem, the dimension formula in Cohen–Macaulay local rings, the dimension criterion for regular sequences, and finite modules supported in V(I) are killed by a power of I.

nodes.title: Pullback of the class of an effective Cartier divisor
nodes.statement: Let g : X′ → X be a morphism of noetherian formal schemes and D ⊆ X an effective Cartier divisor such that g^{-1}D := V(g^*𝒥_D · O_{X′}) is an effective Cartier divisor of X′, i.e. the pulled-back local equations are nonzerodivisors of the stalks of X′ (for instance X, X′ regular and g^♯ injective on the stalks at points of g^{-1}D). Then g^*[K(D)] = [K(g^{-1}D)] in K_0^{g^{-1}D}(X′), where K(D) = [O_X(−D) → O_X] is the Koszul class, and h(g^*[K(D)]) = [O_{g^{-1}D}] in K′_0(g^{-1}D): Tor_1^{O_X}(O_D, O_{X′}) = 0. Without the nonzerodivisor condition, h(g^*[K(D)]) = [O_{g^{-1}D}] − [Tor_1^{O_X}(O_D, O_{X′})].
hypotheses: The nonzerodivisor condition on X′ is essential.
proofSteps: K(D) is a resolution of O_D (FK.0/formal-regular-immersion); g^* of it is the two-term complex [O_{X′}(−g^{-1}D) → O_{X′}] given locally by multiplication by g^♯(f).
Its H_1 is the annihilator of g^♯(f), which is 0 exactly when g^♯(f) is a nonzerodivisor; its H_0 is O_{g^{-1}D}.
If X, X′ are regular, stalks are domains (FK.0/regular-and-cohen-macaulay-formal-schemes), so an injective g^♯ sends the nonzero f to a nonzero element, a nonzerodivisor.
acceptance: Pulling D back along its own inclusion D → X: the local equation becomes 0, Tor_1 = O_D(−D) ≠ 0, and h(i^*[K(D)]) = [O_D] − [O_D(−D)].

sources.match: For a morphism of regular formal schemes injective on local rings, the preimage of a Cartier divisor is a Cartier divisor, and the pullback of the class of O_D is the class of the structure sheaf of the preimage (by the argument of Zhang's Lemma B.2(i), even when the map is not a closed immersion).

nodes.title: Schemes proper over Spf A live over a thickening
nodes.statement: Let A be a noetherian adic ring with ideal of definition I (for example a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformiser ϖ, I = (ϖ)) and π : W → Spf A a morphism of formal schemes with W a quasi-compact scheme. Then π factors through Spec(A/I^n) ↪ Spf A for some n, π is proper in the sense of EGA III (3.4.1) iff W → Spec(A/I^n) is proper for one (equivalently every) such n, and, assuming π proper, for coherent E on W the higher direct images along W → Spec(A/I^n) are finite A/I^n-modules, independent of n. If A is a complete discrete valuation ring, they have finite length.
hypotheses: W a quasi-compact scheme (discretely ringed), not merely a formal scheme.
A noetherian adic.
For the cohomology and finiteness conclusions π is proper. Factoring a quasi-compact scheme through a thickening alone does not give finite cohomology.
Proper uses EGA’s adic finite-type hypothesis as well as proper reductions. Properness of the induced reduced map alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Morphisms into Spf A correspond to continuous ring maps A → Γ(W, O_W) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence); Γ(W, O_W) is discrete for a scheme, so continuity means some I^n maps to 0 on each affine open, hence on W by quasi-compactness.

Use the adic finite-type definition of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism. For a morphism factoring through Spec(A/I^n), properness is equivalent to properness of the scheme morphism to this thickening; properness is invariant under nilpotent thickenings. Properness of the reduced map alone, for an arbitrary non-adic formal morphism, is not this definition.

Coherence of higher direct images for the proper morphism of noetherian schemes W → Spec(A/I^n) (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.2/proper-pushforward-coherent); a finite module over the artinian ring A/ϖ^n has finite length; changing n composes with a closed immersion, which does not change the modules.
acceptance: P¹_{F_p} → Spf ℤ_p is proper and factors through Spec F_p; Spec ℤ/p^3 → Spf ℤ_p factors through n = 3.
Spf ℤ_p itself is not a scheme, and its global sections ℤ_p have infinite length.
W = A¹_k over Spf A factors through Spec k but H^0(W,O_W) = k[t] has infinite A-length; the cohomology claim must require properness.

sources.match: For W a scheme proper over Spf A with A a complete discrete valuation ring, the higher direct images of coherent sheaves are torsion coherent sheaves and so have finite length.
Spf O_F̆-schemes are O_F̆-schemes on which ϖ is locally nilpotent.
A morphism of locally noetherian formal schemes is proper when it is of finite type and its reduction modulo ideals of definition is a proper morphism of schemes.

nodes.title: The Euler degree of a scheme proper over Spf A
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete discrete valuation ring and π : W → Spf A proper with W a noetherian scheme. The Euler degree is deg_W : K′_0(W) → ℤ, [E] ↦ Σ_i (−1)^i length_A H^i(W, E) = Σ_i (−1)^i length_A R^iπ_*E; equivalently deg_W = length_A ∘ π_*, where π_* : K′_0(W) → K′_0(Spec A/ϖ^n) ≅ ℤ (FK.4/schemes-over-formal-base). It is additive, independent of n, and extends to classes of coherent modules on a formal scheme X formally supported on W (via K_0(Coh_W(X)) ≅ K′_0(W), FK.1/formal-supported-devissage).
hypotheses: W a scheme; the degree is not defined for formal W such as Spf A, whose cohomology has infinite length.
Lengths over A, so a closed point with residue field k′ contributes [k′ : k].
proofSteps: Finiteness and vanishing of H^i for i > dim W by FK.4/schemes-over-formal-base and Grothendieck vanishing.
Additivity: a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves gives a long exact cohomology sequence of finite-length A-modules.
The description length_A ∘ π_* is the parent's formula for proper pushforward on G_0 (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.7/pushforward-euler-class), composed with K′_0(Spec A/ϖ^n) ≅ ℤ by length (dévissage).
acceptance: deg[O_{Spec A/ϖ^n}] = n.
deg[O_{P¹_k}(m)] = m + 1 for P¹_k ⊂ Spf A over the residue field k.
deg[O_{Spec k′}] = [k′ : k] for a finite extension k′ of the residue field.

sources.match: For π : W → Spf A proper with W a scheme, the degree map K′_0(W) → ℤ sends [E] to the alternating sum of the lengths of R^iπ_*E, independent of the representative.
The Euler–Poincaré characteristic χ(X, F) := Σ (−1)^{i+j} length_{O_F̆} H^i(X, H^j(F)) for a finite complex F, when the lengths are finite.

uses.how: the derived Euler–Poincaré characteristic is the degree of the derived intersection
Int(g) is finite because ∆ ∩ g∆ is a proper scheme over Spf O_F̆
Int(L) := χ(N, ^LZ(L)) for L of rank n
Z(L) proper over Spf O_F̆ so Int(L) is finite

nodes.title: The derived Euler–Poincaré pairing χ(X, F ⊗ᴸ G) (B.4)
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete discrete valuation ring, X a regular locally noetherian formal scheme of finite dimension with a noetherian exhaustion, and Y, Z ⊆ X closed formal subschemes such that W := Y ∩ Z is a scheme with a proper morphism π : W → Spf A. For coherent sheaves F on Y and G on Z, the Tor sheaves T_j := Tor_j^{O_X}(i_*F,i_*G) are annihilated by 𝒥_Y + 𝒥_Z, so are coherent O_W-modules. Define χ(X,F ⊗^L G) := Σ_{i,j}(−1)^{i+j} length_A H^i(W,T_j) = deg_W([F] ·^L [G]). This gives a symmetric biadditive pairing K′_0(Y) × K′_0(Z) → ℤ, and through h a pairing K_0^Y(X) × K_0^Z(X) → ℤ given by deg_W h(a ∪ b). It is computed on any noetherian open containing W. For merely formally supported sheaves, define the pairing of their dévissage classes in these groups; the displayed π_* formula does not directly apply to those sheaves. If X is over Spf A compatibly with π, the extension also equals the Euler characteristic of the ambient derived tensor on a proper nilpotent thickening of W. Write ⟨Y,Z⟩_X for the pairing of the structure sheaves. As a later application of FK.2/affine-filtration-product, on affine regular X of pure dimension n the Euler characteristic of a cup product of classes in F^{r_i}_ℚ with Σr_i ≥ n depends only on their Gr^{r_i} images, whenever the common support is a proper scheme.
hypotheses: X regular (finitely many nonzero Tor sheaves).
W = Y ∩ Z a scheme proper over Spf A; if W is only a formal scheme (e.g. Y = Z = V(t) in Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧, W = Spf ℤ_p) the pairing is not defined.

The cohomology formula takes F ∈ Coh Y and G ∈ Coh Z, not merely F ∈ Coh_Y(X), G ∈ Coh_Z(X). For the latter use dévissage. Ambient cohomology for power-annihilated sheaves additionally uses X → Spf A extending the given base map on W.
proofSteps: For genuine O_Y- and O_Z-modules, both annihilator ideals act as zero on Tor: the action through either factor agrees. Thus T_j is a coherent O_W-module, with finite cohomology over A by FK.4/schemes-over-formal-base and uniform finite Tor amplitude by regularity and finite dimension.
Biadditivity from FK.1/tor-pairing and additivity of the degree; symmetry from Tor_comm.
Compatibility with ∪ is FK.1/tor-pairing (homologyClass_cup).
Locality: Tor sheaves and lengths of cohomology of sheaves supported in an open U ⊇ W are computed on U; the noetherian members containing W are cofinal (FK.2/noetherian-exhaustion-k-groups).

For sheaves killed only by powers, first use formal-supported dévissage and biadditivity. When an ambient A-structure is given, Tor is killed by a power of 𝒥_W and lives on some W_N = V(𝒥_W^N), a scheme proper over Spf A: W is a scheme and properness is invariant under nilpotent thickenings. Filtering by 𝒥_W gives equality of its cohomological Euler characteristic with the degree of its dévissage class.

For the affine graded-class application, changing one representative by F^{r_i+1} changes the cup product by F^{Σr_i+1}, which is zero because its index exceeds n. Apply deg_W h; no FK.4 result is an input to the earlier FK.2 theorem.
acceptance: X = Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧ over A = ℤ_p: ⟨V(t), V(t − p^n)⟩ = n.
X = Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧, Y = V(p, t), Z = V(t): Tor_0 ≅ Tor_1 ≅ F_p and the pairing is 1 − 1 = 0, an excess intersection whose Tor_1 survives.

nodes.title: Functoriality and base change of the Euler degree
nodes.statement: (a) For a proper morphism g : W_1 → W_2 of schemes proper over Spf A, deg_{W_2}(g_*a) = deg_{W_1}(a) for a ∈ K′_0(W_1). (b) Let A → A′ be a finite extension of complete discrete valuation rings with ramification index e and residue degree f. If W is a scheme proper over Spf A′, hence over Spf A, then deg_{W/A} = f · deg_{W/A′}. (c) More generally let A → A′ be any flat local map of complete discrete valuation rings with ϖ_A A′ = (ϖ_{A′}^e), allowing an infinite residue-field extension. If W is a scheme proper over Spf A and W′ := W ×_{Spf A} Spf A′ (a scheme proper over Spf A′), then deg_{W′/A′}(a_{A′}) = e · deg_{W/A}(a), where a_{A′} is the flat pullback of a. In particular unramified extensions such as O_F → O_F̆ multiply degrees by 1 under base change.
hypotheses: Part (b) assumes a finite extension of complete discrete valuation rings, with finite residue degree f. Part (c) only assumes a flat local map with finite ramification index e; finiteness of A′ over A is not required.
proofSteps: (a) Leray: π_{W_1*} = π_{W_2*} ∘ g_* on K′_0 (SchemeKTheoryOperations:S.2/g-theory-proper-pushforward with functoriality of pushforward).
(b) For a finite-length A′-module M, length_A M = f · length_{A′} M, since the residue field of A′ has length f over A.
(c) Flat base change of cohomology (Stacks 02KH) gives H^i(W′, E ⊗_A A′) = H^i(W, E) ⊗_A A′, and length_{A′}(M ⊗_A A′) = e · length_A M because A′ ⊗_A k = A′/ϖ_A A′ has length e over A′.
acceptance: W = Spec k: over A′ = A[ϖ^{1/2}] (e = 2, f = 1), W′ = Spec(A′/ϖA′) has degree 2 = e · 1.
W = Spec k′ with [k′ : k] = f regarded over A has degree f, over A′ unramified with residue field k′ degree 1.
For A′ = the completion of the maximal unramified extension of A, e = 1 and base change preserves Euler degree; part (b) does not assert restriction-of-scalars finiteness for this infinite extension.

sources.match: Flat base change: for a flat base change of a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism, cohomology of the pulled-back quasi-coherent sheaf is the base change of cohomology.

The degree of a class on W proper over Spf A is an alternating sum of lengths over A, independent of the representative; its behaviour under change of the discrete valuation ring is the bookkeeping recorded here.

nodes.title: Pairing with zero-dimensional classes: length times generic rank
nodes.statement: Let A be a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k, X a regular locally noetherian formal scheme over Spf A, F a coherent O_X-module formally supported on a zero-dimensional scheme W_F proper over Spf A (so F has finite length and is supported at finitely many closed points x), and G any coherent O_X-module. Then χ(X, F ⊗^L G) = Σ_x length_{O_{X,x}}(F_x) · [k(x) : k] · rk(G_x), where rk(G_x) is the rank of G_x over the domain O_{X,x} (the alternating sum of the ranks in a finite free resolution). In particular χ(X, F ⊗^L G) = 0 whenever G is formally supported in codimension ≥ 1 (for example G = O_D for an effective Cartier divisor D), and χ(X, F ⊗^L ·) on K_0^Z(X) factors through Gr^0. This is the case 'some r_i = dim X' of (B.3), proved without Adams operations.

nodes.title: Pairing with an effective Cartier divisor
nodes.statement: Let A, X be as in FK.4/derived-euler-pairing, D ⊆ X an effective Cartier divisor, and F a coherent O_X-module formally supported on a scheme W proper over Spf A. Then χ(X, F ⊗^L O_D) = deg_W[F] − deg_W[F ⊗ O_X(−D)], with no hypothesis on the position of D relative to W. If moreover ϖF = 0 and F = O_C for a proper curve C over k (a closed formal subscheme which is a proper scheme of dimension ≤ 1 over the residue field), then χ(X, O_C ⊗^L O_D) = deg_C(O_X(D)|_C), the degree of an invertible module on a proper curve (χ(C, L) − χ(C, O_C)), whether or not C ⊆ D.
hypotheses: X regular (any X with D Cartier suffices for the first formula); W a scheme proper over Spf A.
proofSteps: O_D has the locally free resolution 0 → O_X(−D) → O_X → O_D → 0 (FK.0/formal-regular-immersion), so F ⊗^L O_D is represented by [F(−D) → F] and χ(F ⊗^L O_D) = deg[F] − deg[F(−D)].

For ϖO_C = 0, lengths over A are dimensions over k, and deg_W[O_C] − deg_W[O_C(−D)] = χ(C, O_C) − χ(C, L^{-1}) with L = O_X(D)|_C; by the definition of the degree and the rank-one tensor formula on arbitrary proper schemes of dimension at most one (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3/vector-bundle-degree; Stacks 0AYR, 0AYX), deg L^{-1} = −deg L, the difference is deg L.
acceptance: If D meets the proper curve C ⊄ D transversally in r k-rational points, the pairing is r.

Let X be the completion of the total space of O(a) over P¹_{ℤ_p} along the zero section of the special fibre, D the zero section (a Cartier divisor) and C = P¹_{F_p} ⊆ D: O_X(D)|_C ≅ O(a), so the pairing is a although C ⊆ D.

nodes.title: Proper pushforward on K′₀ of formal schemes and the projection formula
nodes.statement: Let p : X′ → X be a proper morphism of noetherian formal schemes (EGA III (3.4.1)). Then p_* : K′_0(X′) → K′_0(X), [F] ↦ Σ_q (−1)^q [R^qp_*F], is a well-defined homomorphism (the sum is finite), functorial for composition, compatible with closed pushforward and, for supports, with the Euler degree: if X′ and X are over Spf A, p respects these maps, Y′ ⊆ X′ is a scheme proper over Spf A and its closed image W = p(Y′) is also a scheme proper over Spf A, then deg_{p(Y′)}(p_*a) = deg_{Y′}(a). If X and X′ are regular of finite dimension, define Lp^* : K′_0(Y) → K′_0(p^{-1}Y), [F] ↦ Σ_j (−1)^j [Tor_j^{p^{-1}O_X}(p^{-1}F, O_{X′})]; then the projection formula p_*(Lp^*a ·^L b) = a ·^L p_*b holds in K′_0(Y ∩ p(Z′)) for a ∈ K′_0(Y), b ∈ K′_0(Z′). For p finite and flat of degree d and a supported on a zero-dimensional scheme, deg(p_*Lp^*a) = d · deg(a).
hypotheses: p proper in EGA’s sense: adic, of finite type, with proper reductions. A proper reduced map alone is insufficient (source issue E3).
Coherence of R^qp_* for proper morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes is EGA III (3.4.2), requested from AdicSpacesPartII:F0.
The projection formula needs the regularity of X (finite Tor dimension) to define Lp^*.

Support degree identities use compatible A-structures and a proper scheme target support W containing p(Y′). For the projection formula, p_* of a supported coherent class is taken by supported dévissage; the result lies in K′_0(Y ∩ p(Z′)).
proofSteps: Use the requested coherent higher-direct-image theorem EGA III₁ (3.4.2), and its inverse-limit comparison (3.4.3) with the Mittag–Leffler condition. To get a uniform finite cohomological bound, cover the noetherian target by finitely many affine formal opens. Over each, choose a finite affine formal cover of its proper preimage. Properness gives separatedness, so intersections are affine; affine coherent acyclicity and the finite Čech complex give a bound independent of F and of the reduction level. Take the maximum of these finite bounds. Additivity follows from the resulting bounded long exact sequence.

Functoriality follows from the bounded coherent Leray spectral sequence of the ringed-space derived pushforwards. For the degree identity on scheme supports use the compatible A-structures and FK.4/euler-degree-base-change (a), with supported dévissage as needed.

Use EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E1/projection-formula for the underlying ringed spaces, with F perfect on the regular finite-dimensional target: Rp_*(Lp^*F ⊗^L G) ≅ F ⊗^L Rp_*G. The comparison is a global derived morphism; its being an isomorphism can be checked locally using bounded finite free models for F. The finite global spectral-sequence Euler identities then give equality in the supported coherent K_0. Do not compare K_0 classes merely by restriction, and do not replace derived tensor over O_X by underived reductions modulo an ideal of definition.
Finite flat case: p_*O_{X′} is locally free of rank d, so locally near the finitely many points of the support p_*Lp^*a = a ⊗ p_*O_{X′} ≅ a^{⊕ d}.
acceptance: p = the identity: p_* = id and Lp^* = id.
The finite flat map Spf ℤ_p⟦s⟧ → Spf ℤ_p⟦t⟧, t ↦ s² (degree 2): for a = [F_p] at the closed point, deg p_*Lp^*a = deg[F_p⟦s⟧/(s²)] = 2.

The map Spf k⟦t⟧ → Spec k has a proper reduced map (a point to a point), but its direct image of O has sections k⟦t⟧, not a finite k-module. It is not adic finite type and is outside this pushforward theorem.

sources.match: For a proper morphism of locally noetherian formal schemes the higher direct images of a coherent module are coherent and are the inverse limits of the higher direct images of its reductions.

The source describes pushforward by alternating coherent higher direct images and uses degree scaling for a finite flat map. Its reduced-map parenthetical in §1.8 omits EGA’s adic finite-type hypothesis; see E3. The theorem here keeps that hypothesis.
